entities.name: Adil Shah
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ali-qoli Khan, commonly known by his regnal title Adil Shah (1719–1749), was the second shah of the Afsharid dynasty of Iran, ruling from 1747 to 1748. Born in Khorasan Province, he was the nephew and direct successor of Nader Shah, the visionary founder of the Afsharid dynasty who had established a powerful centralized state through military conquest and administrative reform.

Adil Shah inherited a vast but politically fragmented empire at a turbulent moment in Persian history. His brief reign of approximately thirteen months came during the waning years of the Early Modern era, a period marked by the age of exploration, the printing revolution, and significant religious reformation across the globe. Though his rule was shorter than his uncle's, Adil Shah attempted to maintain the dynastic legitimacy and territorial integrity that Nader Shah had painstakingly assembled, drawing upon established traditions of dynastic succession and sovereign authority that characterized monarchical systems of the era.

Despite the limited duration of his reign, Adil Shah's death in May 1749 marked a critical juncture in Persian history. His passing contributed to the established dynastic legacies and territorial boundaries of the Afsharid state, and indirectly influenced broader patterns of global exchange networks, modern state formation, and the scientific developments that defined the Early Modern period. Adil Shah's life and reign exemplify the complexities of imperial succession, the challenges of maintaining political systems amid geopolitical competition, and the lasting impacts of empire-building during an era of unprecedented global transformation.
